us.title: Australia's August trade surplus shrinks to A$495M as data center equipment imports surge
us.description: A reading about A$1.5 billion below the poll is a clear miss for a surplus that had already been narrowing, and if the import pattern holds it could weigh on the trade contribution to growth. The composition is more informative than the headline: the imports driving the miss are investment-type goods tied to data center build-outs, so the signal is about capital spending demand more than household consumption. Gold's 20% rebound shows how much monthly export swings can distort the balance, which argues for caution in reading one month as a trend. Softer job vacancies add a note of cooling labour demand, leaving the domestic data mixed. --- Earlier: Australia: RBA says most mortgage holders keep equity even if house prices fall another 20% Australia manufacturing PMI falls to 49.6 as new orders drop for first time since June --- A data center equipment buying spree swamped a gold-led export rebound, pulling Australia's goods surplus well below forecast. Summary: Australia's August goods surplus was A$495 million (US$343.73 million), down from a revised A$1.4 billion in July and well below the A$2.0 billion Reuters poll forecast. Imports rose 5.8% on the month, reversing a 2.5% fall in the prior reading. The import rise was led by a 79% jump in ADP equipment used in data centers, with aircraft shipments also higher. Exports rose 3.7%, recovering from a 3.3% drop, with non-monetary gold up 20%. Separate data showed job vacancies fell 0.9% on the quarter after a 2.1% decline previously. Australia's goods trade surplus narrowed sharply in August as a surge in imports of data center equipment overwhelmed a rebound in gold exports, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reported on Thursday. The balance on goods was a surplus of A$495 million (US$343.73 million), down from a revised A$1.4 billion in July and well short of the A$2.0 billion surplus forecast in a Reuters poll. Imports rose 5.8% on the month, reversing a 2.5% fall in the prior reading. The increase was led by a 79% jump in ADP equipment used in data centers, with a rise in aircraft shipments also contributing. Reuters noted that imports of data center equipment had boomed again, which points to a continuing build-out and not a one-off delivery. Exports rose 3.7%, recovering from a 3.3% drop in the previous reading, with non-monetary gold up 20%. The gold rebound was sharp but not large enough to offset the import increase, leaving the surplus about A$1.5 billion below the forecast. The mix of the move matters for how the data is read. Data center equipment and aircraft are investment-type purchases and not everyday consumer goods, and gold exports can swing sharply from one month to the next. That suggests the headline shift in the balance says more about a few specific categories than about a broad change in trade momentum, although the size of the data center jump makes it hard to dismiss as noise. Separate data showed Australian job vacancies fell 0.9% on the quarter, following a 2.1% decline in the previous reading. Two consecutive falls suggest demand for workers is cooling. Attention now turns to whether imports of data center equipment stay elevated in the next monthly report, whether gold exports hold their rebound or give it back, and whether vacancies keep falling. A repeat of the import surge would keep pressure on the surplus, while a fade in both gold and equipment flows would show the August result was driven by timing. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

pt.title: Regras próprias para cartões de saúde
pt.description: A deputada oliveirense Helga Correia defendeu na Assembleia da República a criação de um regime jurídico específico para os cartões de descontos em saúde, considerando que a legislação atual não garante uma proteção suficientemente clara para quem adere a estes produtos. Nota de Imprensa - Helga Correia A posição foi assumida numa audiência parlamentar com a Associação Portuguesa de Planos de Saúde, realizada a 9 de setembro na Comissão de Economia e Coesão Territorial. O diploma pretende criar um Regime Jurídico de Proteção dos Consumidores no âmbito dos Cartões de Descontos em Saúde, produtos que funcionam mediante o pagamento de uma prestação periódica e dão acesso a uma rede de prestadores convencionados. O custo do ato de saúde continua, contudo, a ser suportado pelo beneficiário. Nota de Imprensa - Helga Correia Uma das preocupações destacadas por Helga Correia prende-se com a possibilidade de estes cartões serem confundidos com seguros de saúde. Segundo a deputada, nos cartões de descontos não existe transferência de risco para uma entidade financeira nem cobertura das despesas de saúde por parte da entidade promotora. A parlamentar considera, por isso, necessário tornar mais clara a informação disponibilizada ao consumidor.

pt.title: EMUSA abriu as portas à comunidade
pt.description: “O objetivo principal é dar a conhecer à sociedade os instrumentos musicais” e incentivar os participantes a aprender um instrumento e a desenvolver novos gostos, explicou Tiago Oliveira. Este ano, a escola procura reforçar sobretudo a aprendizagem dos metais graves, embora a escolha do instrumento fique ao critério de cada aluno. Formação ajuda a garantir continuidade da banda A escola de música assume um papel importante na formação de novos elementos e na continuidade da associação. “É muito importante uma associação ter qualquer escola de música”, salientou Tiago Oliveira, destacando também a vertente de formação pessoal e social dos alunos. Nos últimos anos, vários alunos deram continuidade ao percurso musical. Alguns ingressaram em escolas profissionais e no ensino universitário, enquanto outros conquistaram prémios nacionais e internacionais. “Esse não é o principal objetivo, atenção, mas é sempre bom quando isso acontece”, afirmou. A procura pela aprendizagem da música também tem vindo a crescer. Durante o Open Day, a adesão foi visível, com a sede cheia de professores e participantes interessados em experimentar diferentes instrumentos. Entre os principais desafios estão a angariação de instrumentos e a necessidade de mais apoios. “É uma associação sem fins lucrativos” e, por isso, o reforço de fundos poderá ajudar a assegurar o trabalho desenvolvido pela escola e pela banda, referiu Tiago Oliveira.

gr.title: Tέλος το αυτόφωρο για τους εκπαιδευτικούς: «Μπλόκο» στις συλλήψεις μέσα στα σχολεία
gr.description: Τι προβλέπει η διάταξη του υπουργείου Δικαιοσύνης για εκπαιδευτικούς που αντιμετωπίζουν μηνύσεις για πράξεις κατά την άσκηση των καθηκόντων τους. Αλλαγή στο καθεστώς της αυτόφωρης διαδικασίας για τους εκπαιδευτικούς δρομολογεί το υπουργείο Δικαιοσύνης, με διάταξη που αναμένεται να κατατεθεί στη Βουλή και θα αλλάξει τον τρόπο αντιμετώπισης συγκεκριμένων ποινικών υποθέσεων που προκύπτουν μέσα στα σχολεία. Σύμφωνα με τον σχεδιασμό, εκπαιδευτικοί που βρίσκονται αντιμέτωποι με πλημμελήματα τα οποία συνδέονται αποκλειστικά με την άσκηση των υπηρεσιακών τους καθηκόντων δεν θα οδηγούνται στη διαδικασία του αυτοφώρου. Η αλλαγή αφορά περιπτώσεις που σχετίζονται με διοικητικές αποφάσεις, τη λειτουργία του σχολείου ή το εκπαιδευτικό έργο. Η σχετική νομοθετική πρωτοβουλία που έχει επιβεβαιωθεί από τον υπουργό Δικαιοσύνης Γιώργο Φλωρίδη και έρχεται μετά και από σχετικό αίτημα της Ένωσης Διευθυντών Σχολικών Μονάδων. Τι αλλάζει για τους εκπαιδευτικούς Το βασικό στοιχείο της προτεινόμενης ρύθμισης είναι ότι η υποβολή μήνυσης δεν θα οδηγεί αυτομάτως στην άμεση σύλληψη του εκπαιδευτικού μέσα στον χώρο του σχολείου, στις περιπτώσεις που εμπίπτουν στο νέο πλαίσιο. Η υπόθεση θα εξακολουθεί να εξετάζεται από τις αρμόδιες αρχές, όμως αντί της αυτόφωρης διαδικασίας θα ακολουθείται η τακτική δικαστική οδός. Με αυτόν τον τρόπο επιχειρείται να αποφευχθούν περιστατικά κατά τα οποία εκπαιδευτικοί συλλαμβάνονται μέσα στις σχολικές αίθουσες, παρουσία μαθητών και συναδέλφων, για διαφορές ή καταγγελίες που προκύπτουν στο πλαίσιο της άσκησης των καθηκόντων τους. Δεν καταργείται η ποινική διερεύνηση Μηνύσεις και καταγγελίες θα συνεχίσουν να εξετάζονται από εισαγγελικές και δικαστικές αρχές. Εφόσον προκύπτουν στοιχεία που δικαιολογούν την ποινική διερεύνηση μιας υπόθεσης, αυτή θα συνεχίζεται κανονικά. Η διαφοροποίηση αφορά αποκλειστικά τον τρόπο και τον χρόνο με τον οποίο θα κινηθεί η διαδικασία. Αντί της άμεσης σύλληψης και της κατεπείγουσας εκδίκασης στο πλαίσιο του αυτοφώρου, η υπόθεση θα παραπέμπεται στην τακτική δικαστική διαδικασία. Η αλλαγή αποτελεί ένα από τα ζητήματα που είχαν τεθεί από την Ένωση Διευθυντών Σχολικών Μονάδων προς την πολιτική ηγεσία του υπουργείου Δικαιοσύνης. Ιδιαίτερη έμφαση δίνεται στο γεγονός ότι μια σύλληψη μέσα στο σχολείο δεν αφορά μόνο τον εκπαιδευτικό, αλλά πραγματοποιείται σε έναν χώρο όπου βρίσκονται μαθητές, γεγονός που μπορεί να δημιουργήσει επιπλέον ένταση στη σχολική κοινότητα. Η προωθούμενη ρύθμιση δεν καταργεί την ευθύνη των εκπαιδευτικών ούτε εμποδίζει την απονομή της Δικαιοσύνης. Αλλάζει, σύμφωνα με τον σχεδιασμό, το πρώτο και πιο άμεσο στάδιο της διαδικασίας, ώστε για τις συγκεκριμένες υπηρεσιακές υποθέσεις να μην οδηγούνται οι εκπαιδευτικοί σε σύλληψη μέσα στο σχολείο και η υπόθεση να εξετάζεται μέσω της τακτικής δικαστικής οδού. #ΕΚΠΑΙΔΕΥΤΙΚΟΙ #ΣΧΟΛΕΙΑ #ΣΥΛΛΗΨΗ #ΑΥΤΟΦΩΡΟ

in.title: Debia Expands Merchant Acquiring in Malaysia, Deepening Regional Payment Connectivity
in.description: Debia Malaysia meets Bank Negara Malaysia requirements for commencement, marking the Group's next step in building a Southeast Asian payment ecosystem KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia and SINGAPORE , Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Debia is expanding its merchant acquiring business into Malaysia, marking the next phase of the Singapore-headquartered payments group's regional growth strategy. The expansion follows Debia Sdn. Bhd. ("Debia Malaysia") meeting the expectations and conditions stipulated by Bank Negara Malaysia ("BNM") for the commencement of its merchant acquiring operations. This builds on the In-Principle Approval previously granted by BNM and paves the way for Debia Malaysia to roll out merchant acquiring services across the country. Entry into Malaysia extends Debia's acquiring footprint beyond Singapore, establishing a strategic operational base from which the Group can deepen its participation in Southeast Asia's increasingly interconnected payments landscape. Debia Malaysia will leverage the Group's acquiring capabilities, payment technology, and partner network to support Malaysian businesses across physical and digital commerce. Its integrated platform supports a comprehensive range of payment methods, including major card schemes, QR payments, digital wallets and alternative payment channels. By combining Debia's technology and infrastructure with local market capabilities and strategic partnerships, the Malaysian arm is positioned to respond to the evolving needs of local merchants while strengthening the Group's cross-border connectivity. Derrick Tham, Group Chief Executive Officer of Debia, said: "Malaysia represents a significant milestone in Debia's evolution as a regional payments business. Meeting Bank Negara Malaysia's requirements reflects the rigorous work undertaken to establish strong governance, compliance, and operational foundations for our Malaysian operations. "Our focus now is execution — building a sustainable business in Malaysia, fostering strong local partnerships and delivering practical payment solutions that are relevant to how merchants operate and grow. As commerce becomes increasingly integrated across Southeast Asia, we aim to build Debia with strong local roots and cross-border reach, maintaining the discipline required for long-term scalability." Malaysia marks the next phase of Debia's regional expansion as the Group systematically scales its merchant acquiring and payment infrastructure across Southeast Asia. The Group's regional strategy is centred on establishing robust local operations supported by a shared technology core and extensive payment connectivity, anchored by regulatory compliance, governance, and operational resilience as foundations for sustainable growth. About Debia Debia is a Singapore-headquartered payments technology group providing merchant acquiring and payment solutions to businesses. Debia Pte. Ltd. is licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore as a Major Payment Institution to provide merchant acquisition, domestic money transfer and cross-border money transfer services. Through its integrated payment platform and network of payment partnerships, Debia supports businesses across multiple payment methods and channels. The Group is expanding its presence across Southeast Asia, with Malaysia representing the next stage of its regional development.

ph.title: Debia Expands Merchant Acquiring in Malaysia, Deepening Regional Payment Connectivity
ph.description: Debia Malaysia meets Bank Negara Malaysia requirements for commencement, marking the Group's next step in building a Southeast Asian payment ecosystem KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia and SINGAPORE , Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Debia is expanding its merchant acquiring business into Malaysia, marking the next phase of the Singapore-headquartered payments group's regional growth strategy. The expansion follows Debia Sdn. Bhd. ("Debia Malaysia") meeting the expectations and conditions stipulated by Bank Negara Malaysia ("BNM") for the commencement of its merchant acquiring operations. This builds on the In-Principle Approval previously granted by BNM and paves the way for Debia Malaysia to roll out merchant acquiring services across the country. Entry into Malaysia extends Debia's acquiring footprint beyond Singapore, establishing a strategic operational base from which the Group can deepen its participation in Southeast Asia's increasingly interconnected payments landscape. Debia Malaysia will leverage the Group's acquiring capabilities, payment technology, and partner network to support Malaysian businesses across physical and digital commerce. Its integrated platform supports a comprehensive range of payment methods, including major card schemes, QR payments, digital wallets and alternative payment channels. By combining Debia's technology and infrastructure with local market capabilities and strategic partnerships, the Malaysian arm is positioned to respond to the evolving needs of local merchants while strengthening the Group's cross-border connectivity. Derrick Tham, Group Chief Executive Officer of Debia, said: "Malaysia represents a significant milestone in Debia's evolution as a regional payments business. Meeting Bank Negara Malaysia's requirements reflects the rigorous work undertaken to establish strong governance, compliance, and operational foundations for our Malaysian operations. "Our focus now is execution — building a sustainable business in Malaysia, fostering strong local partnerships and delivering practical payment solutions that are relevant to how merchants operate and grow. As commerce becomes increasingly integrated across Southeast Asia, we aim to build Debia with strong local roots and cross-border reach, maintaining the discipline required for long-term scalability." Malaysia marks the next phase of Debia's regional expansion as the Group systematically scales its merchant acquiring and payment infrastructure across Southeast Asia. The Group's regional strategy is centred on establishing robust local operations supported by a shared technology core and extensive payment connectivity, anchored by regulatory compliance, governance, and operational resilience as foundations for sustainable growth. About Debia Debia is a Singapore-headquartered payments technology group providing merchant acquiring and payment solutions to businesses. Debia Pte. Ltd. is licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore as a Major Payment Institution to provide merchant acquisition, domestic money transfer and cross-border money transfer services. Through its integrated payment platform and network of payment partnerships, Debia supports businesses across multiple payment methods and channels. The Group is expanding its presence across Southeast Asia, with Malaysia representing the next stage of its regional development.

ph.title: PRC slammed over medical malpractice case pile-up, probe pushed
ph.description: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Raffy Tulfo slammed slammed the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) over its slow action on cases involving doctors accused of medical malpractice, some of which have reportedly resulted in the patient deaths. During the Senate budget hearing for the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) and its attached agencies on Wednesday,Tulfo cited a 2017 case in which a patient reportedly died after undergoing several procedures simultaneously. The doctor involved was not placed under preventive suspension, allowing a similar incident to reportedly happen again recently, with the patient suffering the same fate. Tulfo questioned why the case took three years to file and remains unresolved nearly nine years after the reported incident. He said the PRC should have initiated an investigation motu proprio when the first incident was reported and considered placing the doctor under preventive suspension. “How many more patients does the PRC have to wait for to die—10? 100?—before it takes action?” Tulfo said. He argued that earlier action could have prevented another alleged malpractice incident and potentially saved another life. "Let’s not wait for a third person to die before taking action. What if all of you there at the PRC undergo the procedure? I’ll sponsor it. Use my credit card," the senator added. In response, PRC Chairman Charito Zamora said the case was filed with the Board of Medicine in 2021 and remained at the board level. Zamora also said the PRC would conduct its own investigation into the more recent case. The issue resurfaced after a Filipino-American reality television personality sought the National Bureau of Investigation’s help last month in determining the circumstances surrounding his mother’s death a week after she underwent several procedures at a beauty clinic in the Philippines. Labor Secretary Francis Tolentino said he would convene the PRC and the Board of Medicine to launch a fact-finding investigation and determine whether charges should be filed against those who may be held liable. Tolentino said the Department of Labor and Employment would inspect the clinic to determine whether it violated the Labor Code. "We can conduct an immediate inspection of the clinic tomorrow and submit a report to this committee. If it is found to be in violation of Article 128 of the Labor Code, we will be the ones to order its closure," he said.

pk.title: Pakistan, China entering new phase of CPEC: PM
pk.description: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Wednesday that Pakistan and China are entering a new phase of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), shifting the focus to industrialisation, special economic zones, IT and artificial intelligence, agriculture, and mining and minerals. Speaking at a function in connection with the 77th anniversary of the founding of China, being celebrated today (Thursday), the prime minister said CPEC 2.0 would underscore the two countries’ shared commitment to building a more prosperous and developed future for their people. “CPEC is a manifestation of our longstanding friendship and our shared resolve for a more prosperous and developed future for our people,” he said, adding that Pakistan had now entered the next phase of the flagship economic cooperation project. He said particular attention would be given to industrialisation, special economic zones, IT and artificial intelligence, agriculture, mining and minerals under the new phase. Sharif described 2026 as a year of special significance in the shared journey of Pakistan and China, as the two countries are also marking the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations. He said Pakistan-China ties had withstood every test over the decades, including earthquakes, storms and floods. “Our hearts are connected and beat together,” the prime minister said, describing the relationship as a friendship that had endured the passage of time. He congratulated Chinese President Xi Jinping and the Chinese people on the occasion, saying China’s National Day was an opportunity to pay tribute to the perseverance, unity and “indomitable spirit” of the Chinese nation. He said China played an important role in promoting global peace, stability and development, while under President Xi’s leadership the country had made significant advances in human development, science, technology and innovation. The prime minister also described Pakistan-China relations as a cornerstone of Pakistan’s foreign policy. Referring to his meeting with President Xi in May, he said their discussions represented a renewed commitment to the longstanding friendship between the two countries. He added that Pakistan was fully committed to implementing the understandings reached between the leadership of the two countries. Quoting a Chinese saying about a sincere friend in a distant land making that distant land feel close, Sharif said the words aptly reflected the friendship and closeness between Pakistan and China. Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong, who also addressed the ceremony, described China and Pakistan as “all-weather strategic cooperative partners”. He said Pakistan was playing an increasingly important role internationally because of what he described as its principled position, broad global vision and diplomatic insight. The ambassador said Pakistan had supported multilateralism and international cooperation and had played an important role in safeguarding peace and security in the region and beyond. Referring to Prime Minister Sharif’s address to the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, Jiang said the Pakistani premier had strongly defended the country’s national interests and presented Islamabad’s position on international and regional issues. He said Pakistan’s stance had been appreciated by the international community. Copyright Business Recorder, 2026

pk.description: LAHORE: The All Pakistan Textile Mills Association (APTMA) has called on the government to restore a regionally competitive business environment, particularly in energy tariffs, taxation and operating costs, warning that textile exports cannot grow unless these constraints are addressed. Speaking at APTMA’s 67th Annual General Meeting, Patron-in-Chief Dr Gohar Ejaz said the industry could raise exports by more than USD 10 billion within a year if given a conducive environment. The sector currently contributes over 60 percent of Pakistan’s total exports and employs around 10 million people, he said. He said exports had stagnated due to high energy tariffs, heavy taxation and rising business costs. Following sustained efforts by his group, the government had approved regionally competitive electricity and gas tariffs for export-oriented sectors, but the facility was later withdrawn, hurting exports, he added. Dr Gohar also announced an initiative to promote value-added exports. Congratulating the newly elected office-bearers and members of the Central and Zonal Managing Committees, he said it was his group’s 17th consecutive electoral victory at both levels. He noted that the new leadership represents different stages of the value chain “from fibre to fashion,” with the North Zone Chairman coming from the garment sector and being among the major exporters of value-added textiles. Outgoing Chairman Kamran Arshad said the industry’s export potential could not be fully realised unless the cost of doing business became globally competitive. He called for competitive energy rates, a tax system that encourages investment and exports rather than penalising exporters, and greater policy stability. He also urged the government to facilitate imports while protecting the domestic value chain from large-scale dumping, which he said was causing serious injury to local industry. Newly elected Chairman Asad Shafi said Pakistan’s GDP had fallen to around USD 450 billion, with agricultural and industrial output declining significantly, while exports remained below USD 30 billion despite six to seven million births annually. This widening gap, he said, was pushing young Pakistanis to seek opportunities abroad. He attributed the decline in competitiveness to falling cotton production and stagnant exports, noting that electricity costs over 11 cents per kilowatt-hour in Pakistan against around six cents in neighbouring countries. pk.title: FBR busts Rs9.41bn wealth statement fraud
pk.description: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has busted a fraud in which taxpayers illegally revised their old wealth statements to bring unexplained assets worth Rs 9.41 billion into their declared wealth. A criminal case under the Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2010 has been registered, and further cases are being processed. The fraud was unearthed by the Directorate General of Intelligence and Investigation (Inland Revenue) through a detailed analysis of FBR’s database, carried out with the support of Pakistan Revenue Automation Limited (PRAL). The analysis identified 85 taxpayers who, between March 2025 and June 2026, revised their wealth statements for tax years 2014 to 2019 and inserted cash, physical gold, prize bonds, properties and business capital that had never been declared before. The law clearly bars this. Under the explanation to section 116(3) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, a wealth statement cannot be revised after five years from the due date of the original return. Every revision identified was made well beyond this limit. In one case, registered by the Directorate of Intelligence and Investigation (Inland Revenue) Lahore, a taxpayer in Lahore region revised his wealth statement for tax year 2015 in May 2026 and inserted fictitious funds of Rs 102.8 million. He then carried this amount forward through his wealth statements up to tax year 2025 and used it to account for seven properties worth Rs 64.41 million bought in May and June 2026. When asked, he could not explain the source of the funds. The tax sought to be evaded in this case alone exceeds Rs 46 million. Regional Directorates of Intelligence and Investigation (Inland Revenue) have launched 48 criminal inquiries across Pakistan, while proceedings in the remaining cases are under process. The money laundering case has been registered against the taxpayer and any abettors found involved, and further cases are being processed to bring everyone behind the fraud to justice. FBR has made it clear that no one will be allowed to use the tax system to whitewash unexplained wealth. Its data analytics will continue to track such manipulation, and anyone found involved will face the full force of the law, including penalties and prosecution. Copyright Business Recorder, 2026

pk.title: Govt considers allowing private firms to directly import LNG: report
pk.description: KARACHI: Pakistan is considering allowing power plants and other private companies to directly import liquefied natural gas (LNG) as it seeks to shore up energy supplies without adding to the strain on state finances, a person familiar with the matter said on Wednesday. According to a Bloomberg report, two of the country’s LNG import terminals have remained largely idle since March, when the conflict in the Middle East virtually halted shipments from Qatar, Pakistan’s largest LNG supplier. Existing regulations don’t easily allow buyers apart from state-owned Pakistan LNG Ltd to procure cargoes from the spot market. The Energy Ministry’s petroleum division has submitted a proposal to greatly increase the scope to auction unused capacity at the terminals and allow private companies to import LNG directly, according to the person, who asked not to be named as the information isn’t public. A director general for the petroleum division didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. Pakistan GasPort Ltd, which operates one of the terminals, has long called for non-state-owned firms like itself to be allowed to import LNG. The South Asian country has been struggling with rolling blackouts and a fuel shortfall as the near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz for gas vessels drastically cut back its LNG deliveries. While Pakistan has been purchasing some shipments from the spot market to replace lost Qatari flows, prices are more than double pre-war levels, weighing on government finances. pk.description: ISLAMABAD: Gas consumers will face higher household fuel costs in October as the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) has announced big increase in Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) prices. The regulatory has issued a notification, raising the price of LPG per kilogram and the standard domestic and commercial cylinder. Under the revised rates, the price of LPG has been increased by Rs20.68 per kilogram. The price of an 11.8kg domestic LPG cylinder has also increased by Rs244.14, bringing the new price to Rs3,296.23. The latest increase means households relying on LPG for cooking and other domestic needs will have to pay more from October, adding to their monthly fuel expenses. LPG price hike comes ahead of the winter season, when demand for household heating and cooking fuel typically rises. With petrol prices already soaring, the latest increase could add further pressure on household budgets and raise transportation and distribution costs, potentially making everyday essentials more expensive. pg.title: 99 Madang Students Graduate Under UOG Distance Learning Program
pg.description: 99 Madang Students Graduate Under UOG Distance Learning Program/Photo supplied Ninety-nine students have graduated from the University of Goroka's distance education programmes in Madang, following the institution's inaugural Institute of Distance and Flexible Learning graduation ceremony at the Holy Spirit Cathedral Hall. The ceremony celebrated students who completed qualifications in education, business, accounting, tourism and hospitality, reflecting the university's efforts to widen access to higher education beyond its main campus. The graduation was held under a theme focused on empowering distance education to shape Papua New Guinea's development over the next 50 years. Among the qualifications awarded were the Bachelor of Education (In-Service) in School Management, Diploma in Early Childhood Education, Diploma in Business Accounting, Diploma in Business Management and Diploma in Tourism and Hospitality Management. UOG Pro Vice Chancellor Academic, Research and Innovation Dr Mathew Landu challenged the graduates to apply their knowledge and skills towards transforming the country's education system. Dr Landu said the university continued to strengthen the quality of its academic programmes by adhering to Measurement Services Standards and other international regulatory requirements governing educational institutions. University of Goroka Council delegate John Sari said the graduation demonstrated the value of cooperation between educational institutions, provincial authorities and other stakeholders in expanding opportunities for professional development. He thanked the Madang Provincial Government and administration for supporting the delivery of programmes, particularly those aimed at developing teachers and improving access to education within the province. Sari also acknowledged the financial assistance arrangements made possible through the partnership, which help students pursue their academic qualifications. The Institute of Distance and Flexible Learning was established nine years ago by UOG, while a formal Memorandum of Agreement with the Madang Provincial Administration was signed in May this year. The university has established 17 IDFL centres nationwide and intends to expand its distance education network to more provinces to reach additional students.

ae.title: Debia Expands Merchant Acquiring in Malaysia, Deepening Regional Payment Connectivity
ae.description: Debia Malaysia meets Bank Negara Malaysia requirements for commencement, marking the Group's next step in building a Southeast Asian payment ecosystem KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia and SINGAPORE , Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Debia is expanding its merchant acquiring business into Malaysia, marking the next phase of the Singapore-headquartered payments group's regional growth strategy. The expansion follows Debia Sdn. Bhd. ("Debia Malaysia") meeting the expectations and conditions stipulated by Bank Negara Malaysia ("BNM") for the commencement of its merchant acquiring operations. This builds on the In-Principle Approval previously granted by BNM and paves the way for Debia Malaysia to roll out merchant acquiring services across the country. Entry into Malaysia extends Debia's acquiring footprint beyond Singapore, establishing a strategic operational base from which the Group can deepen its participation in Southeast Asia's increasingly interconnected payments landscape. Debia Malaysia will leverage the Group's acquiring capabilities, payment technology, and partner network to support Malaysian businesses across physical and digital commerce. Its integrated platform supports a comprehensive range of payment methods, including major card schemes, QR payments, digital wallets and alternative payment channels. By combining Debia's technology and infrastructure with local market capabilities and strategic partnerships, the Malaysian arm is positioned to respond to the evolving needs of local merchants while strengthening the Group's cross-border connectivity. Derrick Tham, Group Chief Executive Officer of Debia, said: "Malaysia represents a significant milestone in Debia's evolution as a regional payments business. Meeting Bank Negara Malaysia's requirements reflects the rigorous work undertaken to establish strong governance, compliance, and operational foundations for our Malaysian operations. "Our focus now is execution — building a sustainable business in Malaysia, fostering strong local partnerships and delivering practical payment solutions that are relevant to how merchants operate and grow. As commerce becomes increasingly integrated across Southeast Asia, we aim to build Debia with strong local roots and cross-border reach, maintaining the discipline required for long-term scalability." Malaysia marks the next phase of Debia's regional expansion as the Group systematically scales its merchant acquiring and payment infrastructure across Southeast Asia. The Group's regional strategy is centred on establishing robust local operations supported by a shared technology core and extensive payment connectivity, anchored by regulatory compliance, governance, and operational resilience as foundations for sustainable growth. About Debia Debia is a Singapore-headquartered payments technology group providing merchant acquiring and payment solutions to businesses. Debia Pte. Ltd. is licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore as a Major Payment Institution to provide merchant acquisition, domestic money transfer and cross-border money transfer services. Through its integrated payment platform and network of payment partnerships, Debia supports businesses across multiple payment methods and channels. The Group is expanding its presence across Southeast Asia, with Malaysia representing the next stage of its regional development.

ae.title: Dubai real estate transactions hit Dh574 billion in nine months - second highest sales value in market history
ae.description: Dubai: Dubai’s real estate market continued its strong performance, with real estate transactions exceeding Dh574.12 billion during the first nine months of 2026, a clear indication of continued market activity and increasing demand for various types of real estate assets, with continued investment flow, in addition to the diversity of buyer segments and high demand for residential units and new projects. Dubai real estate transactions during the period from January to the end of September last year amounted to Dh574.12 billion, through the execution of 165,018 transactions, representing the value of transactions representing about 62.47% of the total value recorded during the whole of 2025, which amounts to Dh919 billion. A survey conducted based on data from the Dubai Land Department showed that Dubai real estate sales from the beginning of this year until the end of last September amounted to about Dh379.4 billion, recording the second highest sales value in the history of the Dubai real estate market, after the figure achieved in 2025. According to the survey, the sales were distributed over 123,416 transactions, including 104,198 transactions for residential units, 9,514 transactions for buildings, in addition to 9,704 transactions for land. Sales of ready-built properties accounted for the largest share of total sales, amounting to Dh196.08 billion, through the execution of approximately 39,320 transactions, distributed as follows: 27,020 transactions for residential units, 2,605 transactions for buildings, and 9,704 transactions for land. In contrast, off-plan property sales reached Dh183.32 billion, through 84,090 transactions, distributed as follows: 77,180 transactions for residential units, and 6,909 transactions for buildings. Mortgage transactions totalled Dh151.13 billion, through 34,910 transactions, distributed as follows: 22,060 transactions for residential units, 4,223 transactions for buildings, and 8,627 transactions for land. The value of the donations amounted to Dh43.6 billion, through the execution of 6,692 transactions, distributed as follows: 5,133 transactions for residential units, 431 transactions for buildings, and 1,128 transactions for land. Business Bay topped the list of the highest-selling areas during the first nine months of this year, with a value exceeding 20 billion dirhams, followed by Airport City with approximately 17.72 billion dirhams, then Al Yalayis 1 with Dh16.09 billion, followed fourthly by Palm Deira with Dh12.98 billion, and fifthly by Palm Jumeirah with Dh11.61 billion. The Me’aisem 2 area came in sixth with Dh11.5 billion, followed by Jumeirah Village Circle in seventh with Dh10.29 billion, then Palm Jebel Ali in eighth with Dh9.4 billion, and the Burj Khalifa area in ninth with Dh8.86 billion, while the Sheikh Mohammed Bin Rashid Gardens area came in tenth with a value of Dh8.5 billion. On a monthly performance level, Dubai real estate sales during September exceeded Dh29.66 billion, through the execution of 11,430 transactions, distributed as follows: 9,744 transactions for residential units, 777 transactions for buildings, and 910 transactions for land. Sales were distributed as follows: Dh16.03 billion for ready properties, through 3,955 transactions, while off-plan property sales amounted to Dh13.63 billion through the execution of 7,476 transactions. Mortgage transactions amounted to Dh16.79 billion, through 4,266 transactions distributed as follows: 2,602 transactions for residential units, 621 transactions for buildings, and 1,043 transactions for land. Gifts totaled Dh4.33 billion through 796 transactions, comprising 616 residential unit transactions, 52 building transactions, and 128 land transactions. This brings the total value of real estate transactions during September to over Dh50.78 billion, across 16,490 transactions.

tr.title: Parayı yatırınca sorular bitmez
tr.description: Fon krizinde çoğunluk birikimi vurguna takılan yatırımcının anaparasını geri alıp alamayacağı üzerine tartışıyor. Peki ya bu düzen büyürken denetlemekle görevli olanların sorumluluğu ne olacak? BIST, BDDK, MKK ve SPK’da görevdeki başkan ve üyelerinin, yöneticilerinin denetim sorumluluğunun hangi bağımsız incelemeye konu edildiği kamuoyuna açıklanmadı. Bir incelme olup olmadığını dahi bilmiyoruz. SPK özelinde Kurul, başka kişilerin işlemleri hakkında kararlar alıyor. Kendi bildiklerini, yaptıklarını, yapmadıklarını ise kim araştırıyor? Bu soruyu sormak için SPK’nın kendi açıklaması yeterli. Kurul, 18 Eylül tarihli açıklamasında, bazı fonların ekonomik gerçeklikle açıklanamayacak fiyat hareketlerine yol açtığını 2025’in son çeyreğinde gözlemlediğini bildirdi. Konu, 2 Aralık 2025’te Finansal İstikrar Komitesi’nde görüşülmüş. Demek ki tehlike aylar öncesinden biliniyormuş. O aylarda hangi hesaplar incelendi? Hangi işlemler durduruldu? Kimler uyarıldı? Yeni yatırımcıların bu manipülasyona takılmasını engellemek için hangi tedbirler alındı? SPK’nın 28 Ağustos düzenlemesini izleyen dönemde, yoğunlaşmış portföyler ve artan para çekme talepleri üzerindeki baskı büyüdü. Pusula’nın 15 Eylül’de bazı fonlarında ödeme temerrüdü açıklamasıyla sorun görünür hale geldi. Bu kronoloji, düzenlemenin tek başına krizi yarattığını değil, önceden birikmiş kırılganlığın ne kadar ciddi olduğunu gösteriyor. Tam burada Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya ve eşi İlyas Kaya’nın işlemleri hakkındaki iddialara bakmak gerekiyor. Kamuoyuna açıklanan rakamlara göre çift, Özata Denizcilik hisselerine yaklaşık 163 milyon lira yatırıyor; birkaç ay sonra yaklaşık 2 milyar 170 milyon liralık satış geliri elde ediyor. “Affını” istemesinden, bu rakamların doğrulandığını anlıyoruz. Fakat iddianın büyüklüğü, açıklama ve inceleme yükümlülüğünü ortadan kaldırmıyor; ağırlaştırıyor. Piyasa tecrübem bana bu büyüklükte parayı tek bir hisseye bağlamanın ciddi bir yoğunlaşma ve likidite riski almak olduğunu söylüyor. Özellikle de çıkarken aynı büyüklükte alıcı bulup bulamayacağınız belirsizse. Bir hisseye-yüklü de olsa- yatırımdan doğrudan “suç işlenmiştir” sonucu çıkmaz. Ama şu soruyu sormamak da mümkün değil: Bu güven nereden geliyordu? Yalnızca şirketin geleceğine duyulan inançtan mı? Birilerinin verdiği kazanç vaadinden mi? Gerektiğinde hisseleri alacak bir karşı tarafın hazır olduğu düşüncesinden mi? Burada bir suç olabileceğine dair makul şüpheyi yaratan da zaten hisseden çıkışın zamanlaması. Kaya’nın hisselerini Tera’ya satarak çıktığı iddiası kamuoyunda dile getirildi. Ancak net bilgi halen gölgelerde. Emir kayıtları, müşteri hesapları ve takas verileriyle kimin kime, hangi fiyatla, hangi saatte satış yaptığı belirlenebilir. Araştırılması gerekenler var: Küçük yatırımcı içeride kalırken kimler çıkabildi? Çıkış kararını hangi bilgiyle verdi? Yaklaşan müdahaleler veya şirketlerin ödeme gücü hakkında kamuya açıklanmamış bilgiye erişenler var mıydı? Bana göre işlem büyüklüğü ile zamanlamanın birlikte ortaya çıkardığı tablo, içeriden bilgi ihtimalinin ciddiyetle araştırılmasını gerektiriyor. Bilginin SPK içinden sızıp sızmadığı da bu araştırmanın dışında bırakılamaz. Ancak kaynağı peşinen belirleyemeyeceğimize göre; şirketler, aracı kurumlar ve diğer bilgi sahibi çevreler HTS kayıtları ve MASAK para trafiği açısından incelenmeli. Şimdi bu soruların önüne “para iade edildi” haberi konuluyor. Haberlerde Kaya çiftinin yaklaşık 2,2 milyar lirayı Hazine hesabına aktardığı belirtiliyor. Ödemenin resmî tutarı, açıklaması ve hukuki dayanağı kamuoyuna gösterilmeden bundan bir aklanma sonucu çıkarılamaz. Çünkü kanunda birbirinden farklı suçlar ve sonuçlar var. Sermaye Piyasası Kanunu’nun 106. maddesi, kamuya açıklanmamış ve yatırım kararını etkileyebilecek bilgiye dayanarak işlem yapıp menfaat sağlamayı düzenliyor. 107’nin birinci fıkrası ise fiyat, arz veya talep hakkında yanıltıcı izlenim yaratmayı amaçlayan işlemleri kapsıyor. İçeriden bilgiyle işlem yapmak ile piyasayı yanıltıcı işlemlerle yönlendirmek aynı suç değil. Bu ayrım, ödeme yapıldıktan sonra da önemini koruyor. 107/3’teki özel pişmanlık imkânı, işlem bazlı piyasa dolandırıcılığı için öngörülmüş. Menfaatin iki katının Hazineye ödenmesi, diğer şartlarla birlikte, soruşturma başlamadan önce gerçekleşirse ceza verilmemesini sağlayabiliyor. Soruşturma başladıktan sonra ise yalnızca ceza indirimi söz konusu. 106. maddedeki bilgi suistimali için aynı ödeme yolu yok. Özata işlemleri nedeniyle Emre Tezmen dahil 11 kişi hakkında 107/1’den suç duyurusunda bulunulması, Kaya’nın işlemlerinin de aynı maddeyle sınırlı incelenmesini gerektirmiyor. Kamuya açıklanmamış bilgiye dayanarak satış yapıldığı şüphesine karşılık 106. maddedeki bilgi suistimali ayrıca araştırılmalı. Keza bu suç bakımından, menfaatin iki katını Hazineye yatırarak cezai sorumluluktan kurtulmayı sağlayan özel bir pişmanlık hükmü yok. İçeriden bilgi iddiası araştırılmadan, dosyanın yalnızca ödeme karşılığında cezasızlık imkânı bulunan 107/1 üzerinden ele alınması eksik kalır. Tabi SPK bir suç duyurusu söz konusu çift için de yapacaksa. Dolayısıyla “parasını yatırdı, konu kapandı” denilemez. Zaten menfaat 2,1 milyar lira olarak tespit edilirse, iki katı 4,2 milyar. Ödenen 2,1 milyarsa, gereken tutarın yarısı. Fakat burada da satış hasılatını, anaparayı ve suçtan kaynaklanan menfaati birbirine karıştırmamak gerekiyor. Hesabı, dayanağı ve kişi bazındaki sorumluluğu açıklamak SPK’nın işi. Kurulun yapacağı başvurunun hangi fiilleri kapsadığı bu nedenle belirleyici önem taşıyor. Kanunun 115. maddesi bu suçlarda soruşturmayı SPK’nın savcılığa yazılı başvurusuna bağlıyor. Ancak hukuki nitelendirme ve nihai karar savcılık ile mahkemenin yetkisinde. Bunca fon mağduru varken olayı yalnızca ödeme kolaylığı bulunan bir suç başlığı altında ele alıp içeriden bilgi ihtimalini incelemeden bırakmak kabul edilemez. ml.title: Rage : vaccination des chiens et prise en charge immédiate des morsures
ml.description: © Internet Le Mali marque ce lundi 28 septembre la vingtième Journée mondiale de lutte contre la rage. Le Conseil des ministres a annoncé une cérémonie à Bamako, sous le thème « Plus forts ensemble ». Selon le gouvernement, la journée est consacrée à la sensibilisation des propriétaires d’animaux de compagnie et à leur vaccination régulière. L’action s’inscrit dans l’objectif international de mettre fin, d’ici à 2030, aux décès humains provoqués par la rage transmise par les chiens. La rage est une maladie virale qui attaque le système nerveux central. Elle se transmet par la salive d’un animal infecté, principalement lors d’une morsure ou d’une griffure. Un contact de la salive avec une plaie ouverte ou une muqueuse constitue également une exposition. Les chiens à l’origine de 99 % des cas humains D’après la fiche publiée le 17 septembre 2026 par l’Organisation mondiale de la santé, les chiens sont responsables de 99 % des cas de rage humaine. Les enfants de 5 à 14 ans figurent parmi les victimes fréquentes. L’OMS estime à 44 203 le nombre annuel de décès dans le monde, sur la base de ses estimations sanitaires de 2021. Elle précise que le décompte exact demeure difficile en raison des cas mal diagnostiqués ou absents des systèmes de surveillance. Quand les symptômes cliniques apparaissent, la maladie est mortelle dans pratiquement 100 % des cas. Le délai entre l’exposition et les premiers signes atteint généralement deux à trois mois, avec des variations allant de moins d’une semaine à un an. Au Mali, le ministère de l’Élevage et de la Pêche indiquait que la maladie était endémique. En citant la Direction générale de la santé et de l’hygiène publique, le département avait recensé onze décès entre janvier et septembre 2024. Ce chiffre constitue un bilan limité à cette période. Un état d’avancement de la campagne de vaccination, publié par l’Agence malienne de presse le 20 mars 2025, faisait état de 523 chiens vaccinés contre la rage à l’échelle nationale. Le chef de la section de surveillance épidémiologique de la Direction nationale des services vétérinaires précisait que les vaccins destinés aux chiens et aux chats étaient importés et facturés entre 15 000 et 20 000 FCFA selon le prestataire. Les gestes après une exposition Après une morsure ou une griffure par un animal potentiellement infecté, l’OMS recommande de laver immédiatement la plaie à l’eau et au savon pendant au moins quinze minutes. La personne exposée doit ensuite consulter rapidement un service de santé. La prophylaxie post-exposition comprend une évaluation de la blessure et une vaccination antirabique complète. Pour les morsures profondes, les griffures ayant traversé la peau ou la contamination d’une muqueuse par la salive, le protocole peut inclure des immunoglobulines ou des anticorps monoclonaux antirabiques. L’OMS classe les griffures superficielles sans saignement parmi les expositions nécessitant un nettoyage et une vaccination immédiate. Les morsures ou griffures ayant traversé le derme relèvent de la catégorie des expositions graves. La vaccination des chiens interrompt la transmission du virus à sa source. L’OMS la présente comme la stratégie la plus rentable pour prévenir la rage humaine. La conduite recommandée après une exposition repose sur trois actes successifs : laver la plaie pendant au moins quinze minutes, se rendre dans une structure sanitaire et suivre entièrement le protocole prescrit. Massiré Diop

mg.title: COMMERCE - Les particuliers se lancent dans l’import-revente
mg.description: Applications, agences, réseaux sociaux : acheter à l’étranger pour revendre à Madagascar n’est plus réservé aux grandes structures. Mais entre délais de 45 à 60 jours, coût du transport et qualité incertaine, la rentabilité est loin d’être garantie. Des marchandises importées transitent par le port de Toamasina avant leur acheminement vers les revendeurs. DEPUIS quelques années, l’import-revente est devenu accessible aux particuliers à Madagascar. Jeunes ou salariés s’appuient sur des applications ou des agences pour commander des produits, principalement en Chine, avant de les écouler localement, souvent via les réseaux sociaux. Si la pratique permet de débuter avec des volumes réduits, elle impose aussi des contraintes financières, logistiques et qualitatives. Pour s’approvisionner, deux options principales s’offrent aux acheteurs : effectuer directement leurs démarches sur des applications dédiées, ou faire appel à des agences intermédiaires gérant l’achat et le fret jusqu’à Madagascar. L’accès aux fournisseurs internationaux s’est ainsi démocratisé pour quiconque souhaite tester ce marché. Une agence spécialisée confirme cet engouement : « Nous sommes installés depuis 2020, mais nous constatons ces derniers temps une forte hausse des demandes et un intérêt croissant pour l’importation », explique son responsable. Sa clientèle va du particulier commandant quelques pièces aux entreprises acheminant des volumes plus importants, acheminés notamment par le port de Toamasina. Formations Les réseaux sociaux servent également de tremplin aux débutants. Des formations y sont proposées dès 15 000 ariary pour apprendre à maîtriser le processus d’achat. Cependant, le secteur manque parfois de sérieux. « J’ai payé 30 000 ariary pour un module, mais après m’avoir fait attendre, on ne m’y a jamais donné accès », dénonce une participante. Autre écueil : la qualité de la marchandise. Les photos et fiches descriptives ne garantissent pas toujours la conformité du produit final. « On commande parfois un peu à l’aveugle. Il est difficile de savoir exactement ce qu’on va recevoir », confirme Solonantenaina, revendeur. À cela s’ajoute la gestion des délais et des coûts. L’agence partenaire indique qu’il faut compter généralement entre 45 et 60 jours d’acheminement. Le prix du transport varie selon le volume commandé : autant de paramètres à intégrer rigoureusement dans le calcul des marges et du prix final. L’import-revente offre ainsi aux particuliers une porte d’entrée vers le commerce international sans nécessiter de lourdes structures. Mais si les opportunités se multiplient, la viabilité de l’activité repose sur une gestion stricte du choix des produits, des frais de transport et des délais de livraison. Fanilo Mampianintsoa

mg.title: IMMOBILIER À ILAFY - Un crédit pour faciliter l’achat d’un logement
mg.description: Sipem Banque, Maison & Tradition et Solidis présentent leur collaboration. À Antananarivo, les prix de l’immobilier et les ressources des ménages freinent souvent l’accession à la propriété. Les solutions de financement peuvent aider certains particuliers à concrétiser leur projet. Devenir propriétaire reste un objectif pour de nombreux ménages. Entre l’achat du terrain, la construction et l’aménagement, réunir la somme nécessaire peut toutefois s’avérer difficile. Le crédit permet de répartir cette dépense sur plusieurs années. Dans ce contexte, Sipem Banque et le promoteur immobilier Maison & Tradition ont annoncé, le 29 septembre à Antananarivo, leur collaboration autour d’un programme résidentiel situé à Ilafy. Solidis participe également au dispositif en apportant une garantie aux financements immobiliers. Le projet prévoit des logements de 144 et 169 mètres carrés, construits sur des terrains d’environ 500 mètres carrés. Il s’inscrit dans l’extension des zones résidentielles autour de la capitale. Le crédit immobilier Tranosoa peut financer l’acquisition ou la construction d’un logement. Selon les conditions applicables à chaque dossier, les prêts peuvent être remboursés sur dix à quinze ans. Les ménages éligibles peuvent ainsi étaler le coût de leur projet. L’accès à la propriété dépend cependant de plusieurs facteurs : les revenus et la capacité d’endettement des ménages, le coût des matériaux et la disponibilité des terrains. Le crédit peut faciliter un achat, mais son obtention reste liée à la situation financière de chaque demandeur. En associant une offre immobilière, un financement et une garantie, les partenaires cherchent à simplifier certaines étapes de l’accession à la propriété. La portée de ce dispositif dépendra de sa capacité à répondre aux besoins et aux moyens des ménages. Lucia Rabarijaona
